headline: Sales and adjusted profit grow as guidance is raised
summary_short: Becton Dickinson's fiscal 2026 third-quarter (our shard's FY2026 Q2) revenue rose 5.4% y/y to $4.98B and adjusted diluted EPS grew 4.9% y/y to $3.23, but total-company reported diluted EPS fell 31.5% y/y to $1.37 as a $74M discontinued-operations loss weighed on the figure.
summary_long: Revenue grew 5.4% y/y (4.4% FXN) to $4.98B, with all four segments up — BioPharma Systems +6.6%, Interventional +6.4%, Connected Care +4.9%, Medical Essentials +4.5% — and US growth (+6.9%) ahead of International (+3.2%). Operating income fell 10.3% y/y to $663M as R&D (+12.0%) and separation-related other operating expense (+544.7%) outgrew revenue. Net income fell 34.3% y/y to $377M, entirely a discontinued-operations swing tied to the Waters spin-off recast; continuing-operations net income held flat at $451M. Long-term debt fell 22.9% y/y to $13.51B on the spin-off distribution. BD raised full-year guidance: revenue toward the high end of its range, adjusted diluted EPS midpoint raised to $12.62-$12.72 from $12.52-$12.72.

drivers.explanation: Growth was broad-based across all four segments (BioPharma Systems +6.6%, Interventional +6.4%, Connected Care +4.9%, Medical Essentials +4.5%), with US revenue (+6.9%) outpacing International (+3.2%).

Y/y decline is explained by cost growth outpacing revenue: R&D rose 12.0%, S&A rose 8.4%, and other operating expense rose 544.7% (separation-related items from the Waters spin-off), against 5.4% revenue growth.

The y/y decline is not from continuing operations (flat at $451M) but from a swing in discontinued operations to a $74M loss from $123M of income a year ago, reflecting the recast for the Biosciences/Diagnostic Solutions spin-off into Waters.
